alt: A word is copied into an empty string one character at a time with result += ch. Each step marks the character being added and shows the new, longer result string above the cells, with a caption counting the old characters Python copies to build it. Presets use a three-letter word, a seven-letter word and a single letter.

steps.caption: `ch` is "c". `result += ch` builds a new string, "c", from the empty string and this one character.
`ch` is "a". `result += ch` builds a new 2-character string: Python copies the 1 old character and adds one.
`ch` is "t". `result += ch` builds a new 3-character string: Python copies the 2 old characters and adds one.
The loop is over. `result` is "cat". It was built as 3 separate strings, each one longer than the last.
`ch` is "p". `result += ch` builds a new string, "p", from the empty string and this one character.
`ch` is "u". `result += ch` builds a new 2-character string: Python copies the 1 old character and adds one.
`ch` is "m". `result += ch` builds a new 3-character string: Python copies the 2 old characters and adds one.
`ch` is "p". `result += ch` builds a new 4-character string: Python copies the 3 old characters and adds one.
`ch` is "k". `result += ch` builds a new 5-character string: Python copies the 4 old characters and adds one.
`ch` is "i". `result += ch` builds a new 6-character string: Python copies the 5 old characters and adds one.
`ch` is "n". `result += ch` builds a new 7-character string: Python copies the 6 old characters and adds one.
The loop is over. `result` is "pumpkin". It was built as 7 separate strings, each one longer than the last.
`ch` is "a". `result += ch` builds a new string, "a", from the empty string and this one character.
The loop is over. `result` is "a". A one-letter word needs only one new string.
